log.reply:
# Proposal: Executive Briefing for Tamarack Instruments

Dear Dana Whitfield,

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal, an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line and AI sales forecasting planned for next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed.

## What the Briefing Covers for the Client

The session maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to the Client's three use cases. These are framed as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. Topics include:

* transparency expectations for the chatbot
* how the visual inspection system may be classified under the EU AI Act
* data protection expectations consistent with the Client's requirement that customer data stay in the EU

United States obligations appear only as a general landscape item, since no US driver is stated.

We will also discuss three practical matters. The first is closing the inventory gap. The second is how consultation with the German works council fits the path to production. The third is how ISO/IEC 42001 relates to the ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 frameworks the Client names. We will not assume what records those systems already hold.

The operating model overview draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Board-layer context comes from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). Throughout, we apply three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

## Logistics and Price

The Executive Briefing is a two-hour live virtual session for executive leadership and board-level attendees. The price is US$3,000.

Roles identified in discovery are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, the German plant manager and two internal auditors. Final attendance is Unknown, and we will confirm it with you.

The Briefing does not provide certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

## What the Client Receives Afterward

The Client receives a written follow-up memo. It summarizes the decisions surfaced and our readiness observations. It also sets out three prioritized recommendations, each with a suggested next program option and timeline.

## Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. If you would like to proceed, reply to confirm. We will then propose session dates and agree attendance with you.

Kind regards,

[Consultant name]
Senior AI Governance Consultant, AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

Mode A allows "no bullet lists". My word count is roughly 440 to 450, which is borderline.

judgment_calls: The word count is borderline at about 440 to 450 depending on how URLs, headings and the title are counted. I did not rely on it for the verdict, because the bullet list fails item 6 on its own.

I treated the works council sentence, the 42001 versus 27001/9001 discussion and the US landscape item as proposed or conditional content, not new Client facts, following the v1.14.3 guidance. Another scorer could read them more strictly, but that would not change the verdict.
score.reasoning: Items 1 to 5 and 7 are met and none of the fail indicators appears. Item 6 is not met: Mode A requires prose only with no bullet lists, and the response puts a three-item bullet list in the "What the Briefing Covers" section. Partial compliance is a FAIL, so the case fails.
